project.name: treetracker-field-data
project.description: Field data service that owns the raw tree tracking data that the Treetracker app uploads: raw captures, sessions, tracks, device configurations, and wallet registrations. A layered Express service (routes, handlers, services, models, repositories) over PostgreSQL, which also writes the legacy tables.

nodes.name: clear-db.js
nodes.summary: Test helper that empties the legacy tree_attributes, trees and planter tables and the field-data raw_capture, track, session, device_configuration and wallet_registration tables, in foreign-key-safe order, before each API spec suite.

nodes.name: clearDB
nodes.summary: Async function that takes the knex and knexLegacyDB clients and deletes all rows from tree_attributes, trees and planter (legacy DB), then raw_capture, track, session, device_configuration and wallet_registration (field-data DB).

nodes.name: device-configuration-api.spec.js
nodes.summary: Mocha and supertest integration spec for the /device-configuration API: POST a fixed device configuration expects 201, a repeated POST expects 200 (idempotent duplicate), and GET list plus GET /device-configuration/:id must return the stored id. It also exports deviceConfigurationObject as a shared fixture for the session and capture specs.

nodes.name: insert-test-capture.js
nodes.summary: Shared capture fixture module: defines captureRequestObject (session_id, lat/lon, gps_accuracy, rotation_matrix, extra_attributes, captured_at), plus capture and captureWithExistingTree variants with fixed UUIDs, and a seeding function that builds the full planter, device, wallet, session, legacy tree and raw_capture chain.

nodes.name: insertTestCapture
nodes.summary: Seeds both databases for capture tests: inserts a legacy planter whose email is the wallet, the device_configuration, wallet_registration and session rows, a legacy trees row for capture.id whose returned id becomes the raw_capture reference_id (status 'unprocessed', extra_attributes wrapped in entries), and a second legacy tree for captureWithExistingTree.

nodes.name: legacy-table-creation.js
nodes.summary: Mocha root-level before hook that runs raw CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS SQL on knexLegacyDB to create the legacy trees (with uuid, status, images, domain_specific_data, PostGIS estimated_geometric_location), tree_attributes and planter tables, so the integration tests can run against an empty legacy database.

nodes.name: raw-capture-api.spec.js
nodes.summary: Integration spec for /raw-captures: covers 201 on first POST, 200 on duplicate POST, 200 for an already approved capture (reference_id 64864), 201 for a new capture whose uuid already has a legacy tree, list and single GET, and PATCH /raw-captures/:id/reject with a sinon stub on LegacyAPIService.rejectLegacyTree that checks the forwarded Authorization header, organizationId and rejectionReason and expects status 'rejected'.

nodes.name: session-api.spec.js
nodes.summary: Integration spec for the /session API: seeds device_configuration and wallet_registration rows, then checks POST /session returns 201, a duplicate POST returns 200, and GET /session plus GET /session/:id return the stored session. It exports sessionObject (bulk_pack_version 'v2', originating_wallet_registration_id, target_wallet) for the track and capture specs.

nodes.name: track-api.spec.js
nodes.summary: Integration spec for the /track API: after seeding via insertTestCapture, POST /track with locations_url, session_id and bulk_pack_file_name expects 201, then GET /track?session_id= must return one track with query count 1, limit 100 and offset 0, and GET /track/:id must return it.

nodes.name: wallet-registration-api.spec.js
nodes.summary: Integration spec for /wallet-registration: POST expects 201, a second registration with the quasi-email 'mobile@test' also expects 201, a duplicate POST expects 200, and list plus single GET return the record. It exports walletRegistrationObject (wallet, grower_account_id, phone, email, v1_legacy_organization) as a shared fixture.

nodes.name: config.js
nodes.summary: Central runtime config that maps the DATABASE_URL env var to connectionString and DATABASE_URL_LEGACYDB to connectionStringLegacyDB for the two Postgres databases, and sets an empty sentryDSN.
nodes.languageNotes: Exports sentryDSN, but server/app.js reads config.sentry_dsn, so Sentry.init receives an undefined DSN.

nodes.name: app.js
nodes.summary: Builds the Express app: initializes Sentry, enables CORS only when NODE_ENV is development, rejects POST/PATCH/PUT requests without an application/json content-type with HttpError 415, serves /assets statically and Swagger UI at /docs, mounts the main router at /, applies the global errorHandler, and answers any unmatched GET with the package.json version.

nodes.name: app.spec.js
nodes.summary: Small supertest spec for server/app.js: GET / must return 200 (the package version fallback) and an empty POST / must return 415 with a message that mentions application/json.

nodes.name: knex.js
nodes.summary: Creates the two Knex Postgres clients: knex for the field-data DB and knexLegacyDB for the legacy treetracker DB. It throws if either connection string does not start with postgresql:/, uses a pool of 0 to 10, enables debug when NODE_LOG_LEVEL is debug, and sets searchPath from DATABASE_SCHEMA on the field-data client only.

nodes.name: connectionObject
nodes.summary: Parses a postgresql://user:pass@host:port/db?ssl=true URL with a regex into a pg connection object with ssl.rejectUnauthorized false, to avoid pg 8 SSL errors on newer Node versions; it returns the raw string when the URL has no ssl=true suffix.

nodes.name: server.js
nodes.summary: Process entry point: loads dotenv from .env.<NODE_ENV>, applies the log level via setup.js, starts the Express app on NODE_PORT (default 3006), and on SIGINT destroys both the knex and knexLegacyDB pools and closes the HTTP server.

nodes.name: setup.js
nodes.summary: Global startup setting module that sets the loglevel default level from NODE_LOG_LEVEL, or to 'info' when the variable is unset.

nodes.name: LegacyTree.js
nodes.summary: Temporary backward-compatibility model that copies a field-data raw capture into the legacy treetracker main DB: it resolves the planter by wallet and writes rows to the legacy trees and tree_attributes tables.
nodes.languageNotes: The header comment documents the intent to delete this model once the monolith DB split is finished; legacy tree_attributes is described as future capture_metadata.

nodes.name: LegacyTree
nodes.summary: Legacy tree builder bound to a LegacySession; maps capture plus session fields to a frozen legacy trees row and inserts it idempotently by uuid together with its tree_attributes rows.

nodes.name: legacyTree
nodes.summary: Looks up the legacy planter whose phone or email equals the wallet and throws HttpError 422 'Legacy planter has not been created for the legacy tree' when none exists; otherwise returns a frozen trees row with lowercased uuid, planter_id, planter_identifier, planter_photo_url, note and time_created/time_updated set from captured_at.

nodes.name: createTreesInLegacyDB
nodes.summary: Returns the existing legacy trees row when one with the same uuid exists; otherwise inserts the tree through LegacyTreeRepository.create and inserts each extra attribute into tree_attributes with tree_id set to the new tree id.

nodes.name: RawCapture.js
nodes.summary: Domain model for field-data raw captures: shapes raw_capture rows into a frozen object, reads them with session, wallet and device joins, creates them idempotently with status 'unprocessed', and marks them 'rejected'.

nodes.name: RawCapture
nodes.summary: Raw capture model class that wraps RawCaptureRepository for one DB session and exposes list, count, get-by-id, create and reject operations that return frozen raw capture objects.

nodes.name: RawCapture
nodes.summary: Static factory that freezes the public raw capture shape: id, reference_id, session_id, step counts, rotation_matrix, image_url, lat/lon, gps_accuracy, wallet and grower_account_id, extra_attributes, status, rejection_reason, captured_at and organization_id.

nodes.name: createRawCapture
nodes.summary: Returns the existing capture with status 200 when raw_capture.id already exists; otherwise inserts the capture with status 'unprocessed' and fresh created_at/updated_at timestamps and returns it with status 201.

nodes.name: rejectRawCapture
nodes.summary: Sets a raw capture row to status 'rejected' with the given rejection_reason and a new updated_at, then returns the previously read capture merged with these updates.

nodes.name: SessionModel.js
nodes.summary: Domain model for field-data sessions: freezes session rows enriched with device_identifier and wallet data, lists and counts sessions, and creates a session only when its id is not already stored.

nodes.name: SessionModel
nodes.summary: Session model class over SessionRepository that provides getSessions, getSessionsCount, getSessionById (limit 1 on session.id) and idempotent createSession, all returning frozen session objects.

nodes.name: SessionModel
nodes.summary: Static factory that freezes the session response shape: start_time, bulk_pack_version, device_configuration_id, originating_wallet_registration_id, target_wallet, check_in_photo_url, track_url, organization fields, wallet fields and created_at.

nodes.name: createSession
nodes.summary: Inserts a new session row with created_at set to now and returns it with status 201, or returns the already stored session with status 200 when the id exists.

nodes.name: BaseRepository.js
nodes.summary: Generic Knex repository base class that every field-data and legacy repository extends; it provides table-scoped getById, nested and/or filter queries with limit/offset, counts, update and insert with runtime result checks.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses expect-runtime assertions on query results instead of a schema validator; filters may nest and/or arrays recursively.

nodes.name: BaseRepository
nodes.summary: Abstract-style repository bound to a table name and a Session; all queries go through session.getDB() so they join the caller's open transaction.

nodes.name: getById
nodes.summary: Selects the first row of the bound table with the given id and throws HttpError 404 'Can not found <table> by id' when no row matches.

nodes.name: getByFilter
nodes.summary: Builds a Knex where clause from a filter object that can nest 'and' and 'or' arrays of single-key conditions, applies optional limit and offset, and asserts that the result is an array.

nodes.name: countByFilter
nodes.summary: Runs a COUNT on the bound table with a plain where filter, asserts the Postgres string count shape and returns it parsed as an integer.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Updates the row whose id equals object.id with the given fields, returns the updated row via RETURNING *, and asserts that a row with an id came back.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Inserts the given object (or array of objects) into the bound table with RETURNING *, asserts that the first result has an id, and returns that first row.

nodes.name: PlanterRepository.js
nodes.summary: Legacy repository for the treetracker main DB planter table that finds a planter whose phone or email matches a wallet identifier.

nodes.name: LegacyPlanterRepository
nodes.summary: BaseRepository subclass for the legacy planter table whose findUser returns the first planter where phone or email equals the planter identifier.

nodes.name: TreeAttributeRepository.js
nodes.summary: Legacy repository for the treetracker main DB tree_attributes table, used to store per-capture extra attributes next to legacy trees rows.

nodes.name: LegacyTreeAttributeRepository
nodes.summary: BaseRepository subclass bound to tree_attributes; its add method inserts each attribute row in parallel through the inherited create, but LegacyTree calls create with the whole array instead.

nodes.name: TreeRepository.js
nodes.summary: Legacy repository for the treetracker main DB trees table that inserts a tree with a PostGIS point geometry using a raw SQL statement.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses knex.raw with positional bindings because ST_PointFromText cannot be expressed in the Knex insert builder.

nodes.name: LegacyTreeRepository
nodes.summary: BaseRepository subclass bound to the legacy trees table that overrides create with a geometry-aware raw insert.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Inserts a legacy trees row (planter_id, lat, lon, planter_photo_url, planter_identifier, device_identifier, note, uuid, image_url, timestamps) and sets estimated_geometric_location to ST_PointFromText('POINT(lon lat)', 4326), returning the new id.

nodes.name: RawCaptureRepository.js
nodes.summary: Repository for the field-data raw_capture table that reads captures joined with session, wallet_registration and device_configuration, newest first, with optional limit/offset.

nodes.name: RawCaptureRepository
nodes.summary: BaseRepository subclass bound to raw_capture that overrides getByFilter with a three-table left join and adds a CTE-based insert-and-read add method.

nodes.name: getByFilter
nodes.summary: Selects raw_capture columns plus device_identifier, grower_account_id, wallet, user_photo_url and session.organization_id through left joins on session, wallet_registration and device_configuration, ordered by created_at descending with optional limit and offset.

nodes.name: add
nodes.summary: Inserts a raw capture inside a 'createdRawCapture' CTE and selects the new row joined with session, wallet_registration and device_configuration; the RawCapture model uses the inherited create instead, so no caller in server/ uses this method.

nodes.name: SessionRepository.js
nodes.summary: Repository for the field-data session table that reads and counts sessions joined with wallet_registration and device_configuration for wallet and device details.

nodes.name: SessionRepository
nodes.summary: BaseRepository subclass bound to the session table that adds a joined getSessions query and overrides countByFilter so filters may use joined columns.

nodes.name: getSessions
nodes.summary: Selects session columns such as target_wallet, check_in_photo_url, track_url, bulk_pack_version and organization_id plus device_identifier and wallet fields via left joins, applying limitOptions.limit and limitOptions.offset unconditionally.

nodes.name: countByFilter
nodes.summary: Counts session rows after left joining wallet_registration and device_configuration so the filter can reference joined columns, and returns the Postgres count parsed as an integer.

nodes.name: LegacyAPIService.js
nodes.summary: HTTP client for the legacy treetracker admin API at TREETRACKER_LEGACY_API_URL (default http://treetracker-admin-api.admin-api) that rejects a legacy tree.

nodes.name: rejectLegacyTree
nodes.summary: Sends an axios PATCH to /api/[organization/<id>/]trees/<id> with approved=false, active=false and the rejectionReason, forwarding the caller's legacy authorization header.

nodes.name: RawCaptureService.js
nodes.summary: Service that coordinates raw capture use cases across two databases: it writes the legacy trees row and the field-data raw_capture row in paired transactions, and rejects captures through the legacy admin API.
nodes.languageNotes: Coordinates two independent DB transactions (Session and LegacySession) manually; this is not a distributed transaction, so the commit of one can succeed while the other fails.

nodes.name: RawCaptureService
nodes.summary: Raw capture service class instantiated per request by the raw capture handler; it owns a field-data Session and a RawCapture model and passes list, count and get-by-id calls through to the model.

nodes.name: createRawCapture
nodes.summary: Throws HttpError 409 when the capture's session_id is not stored yet; otherwise creates or reuses the legacy trees row in a LegacySession transaction, stores the raw capture with reference_id set to the legacy tree id, commits both, and rolls back any open transaction on error.

nodes.name: rejectRawCapture
nodes.summary: Inside a field-data transaction, reads the capture's reference_id, calls the legacy admin API to reject that legacy tree for the organization, then marks the raw capture rejected and commits, rolling back on failure.

nodes.name: HttpError.js
nodes.summary: Shared error type for the service layers that carries an HTTP status code and a rollback flag; the Express error handler in server/utils/utils.js converts it to an HTTP response.

nodes.name: HttpError
nodes.summary: Error subclass with a numeric code and shouldRollback(); because the constructor uses 'toRollback || true', shouldRollback always returns true even when false is passed.

nodes.name: index.js
nodes.summary: Express handlers for the /raw-captures API: list with filter and limit/offset paging, create a raw capture from the Treetracker app upload, fetch one by raw_capture_id, and reject a capture through the legacy admin API. Each handler validates input with the Joi schemas in ./schemas before it calls RawCaptureService.

nodes.name: rawCaptureGet
nodes.summary: Validates req.query with rawCaptureGetQuerySchema, splits it into filter and limit/offset, reads matching raw captures and their total count from RawCaptureService, and responds with raw_captures, prev/next links for 'raw-captures', and the echoed query with count.

nodes.name: rawCapturePost
nodes.summary: Handles POST /raw-captures: drops extra_attributes from the body (not yet sent by mobile), clamps rotation_matrix entries below 0.001 to 0, validates with rawCaptureSchema, then calls RawCaptureService.createRawCapture and replies with the returned status (201 new or 200 existing) and capture.

nodes.name: rawCaptureRejectPatch
nodes.summary: Handles PATCH /raw-captures/:raw_capture_id/reject: validates rejection_reason/organization_id body and the id param, throws HttpError 422 when the Authorization header for the legacy admin API is missing, and passes the reason, organization, id, and header to RawCaptureService.rejectRawCapture.

nodes.name: rawCaptureSingleGet
nodes.summary: Handles GET /raw-captures/:raw_capture_id: validates the id with rawCaptureIdParamSchema, loads the capture via RawCaptureService.getRawCaptureById, and throws HttpError 404 'raw capture with <id> not found' when no row has an id.

nodes.name: index.js
nodes.summary: Express handlers for the /session API that record and read field data collection sessions: create a session (idempotent on id), list sessions with filters and paging links, and fetch one session by session_id. Validation uses the Joi schemas in ./schemas and data access goes through SessionService.

nodes.name: sessionPost
nodes.summary: Handles POST /session: validates the body with sessionPostSchema, calls SessionService.createSession inside a transaction, and replies with the status the model returns (201 when created, 200 when the session id already exists) and the session.

nodes.name: sessionGet
nodes.summary: Handles GET /session: validates query params with sessionGetQuerySchema, derives filter and limit/offset (default 100/0), fetches sessions and their count from SessionService, and returns sessions, prev/next links built on the 'session' url, and the query with count.

nodes.name: sessionSingleGet
nodes.summary: Handles GET /session/:session_id: validates the param with sessionIdParamSchema, loads the session through SessionService.getSessionById, and throws HttpError 404 'session with <id> not found' when the result has no id.

nodes.name: index.js
nodes.summary: Express handlers for the /wallet-registration API that store grower wallet registrations made on a device: create a registration (requires phone or email), list registrations with filters and paging, and fetch one by wallet_registration_id, all through WalletRegistrationService.

nodes.name: walletRegistrationPost
nodes.summary: Handles POST /wallet-registration: validates the body with walletRegistrationPostSchema, throws HttpError 422 'Either phone or email is required' when both are absent, then calls WalletRegistrationService.createWalletRegistration and returns its status and record as JSON.

nodes.name: walletRegistrationGet
nodes.summary: Handles GET /wallet-registration: validates query params with walletRegistrationGetQuerySchema, reads filtered and paged wallet registrations plus their count, and responds with wallet_registrations, prev/next links for 'wallet-registration', and the query with count.

nodes.name: walletRegistrationSingleGet
nodes.summary: Handles GET /wallet-registration/:wallet_registration_id: validates the id param, loads the record via WalletRegistrationService.getWalletRegistrationById, and throws HttpError 404 'wallet registration with <id> not found' when it is missing.

nodes.name: deviceConfigurationRoutes.js
nodes.summary: Express router for device configurations: maps POST and GET /device-configuration and GET /device-configuration/:device_configuration_id to the deviceConfigurationHandler functions, each wrapped in handlerWrapper so async errors reach the global error handler.

nodes.name: index.js
nodes.summary: Route barrel that exports an array of the five Express routers (device-configuration, raw-captures, session, wallet-registration, track); server/app.js mounts this array at '/'.

nodes.name: rawCaptureRoutes.js
nodes.summary: Express router for raw captures: POST and GET /raw-captures, GET /raw-captures/:raw_capture_id, and PATCH /raw-captures/:raw_capture_id/reject, each bound to a rawCaptureHandler function through handlerWrapper.

nodes.name: sessionRoutes.js
nodes.summary: Express router for sessions: binds POST and GET /session and GET /session/:session_id to sessionPost, sessionGet, and sessionSingleGet, wrapped by handlerWrapper for async error forwarding.

nodes.name: walletRegistrationRoutes.js
nodes.summary: Express router for wallet registrations: binds POST and GET /wallet-registration and GET /wallet-registration/:wallet_registration_id to the walletRegistrationHandler functions via handlerWrapper.

nodes.name: SessionService.js
nodes.summary: Service layer for sessions: builds a Session database context and a SessionModel, prefixes filter keys with 'session.' or 'wallet_registration.' (for grower_account_id and wallet) before list and count queries, and wraps session creation in a begin/commit/rollback transaction.

nodes.name: SessionService
nodes.summary: Class exported as the module that sessionHandler instantiates per request; it holds a Session (Knex transaction wrapper) and SessionModel, and exposes getSessions, getSessionsCount, getSessionById, and createSession.

nodes.name: addTableNames
nodes.summary: Rewrites a session filter object into table-qualified keys: grower_account_id and wallet become wallet_registration.<key>, every other key becomes session.<key>, so the joined session query can filter on both tables.

nodes.name: createSession
nodes.summary: Opens a transaction on the Session context, calls SessionModel.createSession (which returns the existing session with 200 or inserts a new one with created_at and 201), commits, and rolls back on any error before it rethrows.

nodes.name: helper.js
nodes.summary: Pagination helpers shared by the list handlers: getFilterAndLimitOptions separates limit/offset (defaults 100 and 0) from the query filter, and generatePrevAndNext builds relative prev/next URLs with URL-encoded query params.

nodes.name: generatePrevAndNext
nodes.summary: Builds paging links for a list endpoint: encodes the query object (without offset) into '<url>?...&offset=', returns next with offset+limit while the current page index is below count/limit - 1, and prev with offset-limit when it stays at or above 0; null otherwise.

nodes.name: getFilterAndLimitOptions
nodes.summary: Copies req.query into a filter, coerces limit and offset to numbers with defaults of 100 and 0 into limitOptions, and deletes both keys from the filter so only column filters remain.

nodes.name: utils.js
nodes.summary: Global Express error plumbing: handlerWrapper forwards rejected promises from async route handlers to next(), and errorHandler maps HttpError, Joi ValidationError (422), and Axios errors from external calls such as the legacy admin API to JSON {code, message} responses.
nodes.languageNotes: Adapted from express-async-handler; exports are assigned with the CommonJS exports.<name> form, so they are not detected as named function declarations.

nodes.name: handlerWrapper
nodes.summary: Wraps an Express handler so that its return value is resolved as a promise and any rejection or thrown error is passed to the last argument, next(e), letting async handlers throw HttpError directly.

nodes.name: errorHandler
nodes.summary: Express error middleware: logs non-Axios errors, sends err.code for HttpError, 422 with joined Joi detail messages for ValidationError, 500 with the upstream message (and logs the microservice url and data) for Axios errors, and 500 'Unknown error (<message>)' otherwise.

nodes.name: 00_job_database_cleaner.js
nodes.summary: First Knex seed: it empties the field_data tables raw_capture, session, wallet_registration and device_configuration with raw DELETEs, then removes the legacy planter rows whose grower_account_uuid matches a seeded grower account and the trees rows of those planters.

nodes.name: seed
nodes.summary: Runs one raw SQL block that deletes all rows from raw_capture, session, wallet_registration and device_configuration, then deletes planter rows by grower_account_uuid (returning ids) and the trees rows with those planter_id values.

nodes.name: 01_table_device_configuration.js
nodes.summary: Knex seed that inserts one device_configuration row for each of the 100 fixed UUIDs in data/device_configuration.js, with Chance random strings for the device and app fields.

nodes.name: seed
nodes.summary: Inserts the device_configuration rows in parallel with Promise.all; device_identifier, brand, model, device, serial, hardware, manufacturer, app_build, app_version, os_version and sdk_version get random strings, and logged_at and created_at get the current time.

nodes.name: 02_table_wallet_registration.js
nodes.summary: Knex seed that creates 100 wallet_registration rows from the fixed walletRegistrationIds, each one copied from a random grower account in data/wallet_registration.js.

nodes.name: seed
nodes.summary: For each walletRegistrationId, picks a random grower account and inserts wallet, user_photo_url (from image_url), grower_account_id, first_name, phone, lat and lon (default 0), email set to the wallet name and a Chance last_name.

nodes.name: 03_table_session.js
nodes.summary: Knex seed that creates 100 session rows and pairs session i with device configuration i and wallet registration i from the seed data lists.

nodes.name: seed
nodes.summary: Loops i from 0 to 99 and inserts a session row with id sessionIds[i], device_configuration_id deviceConfigurationIds[i], originating_wallet_registration_id walletRegistrationIds[i] and created_at now.

nodes.name: 04_table_raw_capture.js
nodes.summary: Knex seed that loads the 13537 capture-match records into field_data.raw_capture with status 'unprocessed'. For each record it also creates a planter if needed and a matching legacy trees row, and links that row through reference_id.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a Knex CTE (knex.with('createdTree', insert ... returning id)) so the trees insert and the raw_capture insert run as one SQL statement, with reference_id taken from a subselect on the CTE.

nodes.name: createRawCapture
nodes.summary: Picks a random wallet registration and joins it to its session and to public.planter by grower_account_uuid; if no planter exists it inserts one. Then in one CTE statement it inserts a trees row (new uuid, time_created from captured_at, gps_accuracy default 0) and a field_data.raw_capture row with the same id, the session_id, reference_id set to the new tree id and status 'unprocessed'.

nodes.name: seed
nodes.summary: Iterates over every record in capture_match_raw_captures and awaits createRawCapture for each one sequentially, so that planter creation for a grower account happens only once.

nodes.name: capture_match_raw_captures.js
nodes.summary: Generated seed fixture that exports an array of 13537 capture records from February 2022 near Freetown, Sierra Leone (lat about 8.45, lon about -13.17). Each record has an image_url on the treetracker-production-images S3 bucket (eu-central-1), lat, lon, gps_accuracy ('' or 0), note 1, captured_at, time_created and time_updated.
nodes.languageNotes: Plain CommonJS module.exports of a literal array; at about 149k lines it is data, not logic.

nodes.name: device_configuration.js
nodes.summary: Seed fixture that exports a plain array of 100 hard-coded device_configuration UUIDs, used as row ids by 01_table_device_configuration.js and as session foreign keys by 03_table_session.js.

nodes.name: session.js
nodes.summary: Seed fixture that exports sessionIds, a fixed list of 100 UUIDs that 03_table_session.js uses as the primary keys of the seeded session rows.

nodes.name: wallet_registration.js
nodes.summary: Seed fixture that exports growerAccounts (54 treetracker grower accounts with wallet names such as mobile1@test, wallet12 and walletPayToGrow, organization_id, first_name and dummy image_url; only the first six have lat and lon) and walletRegistrationIds (100 fixed UUIDs).

nodes.name: docs.js
nodes.summary: Builds the OpenAPI paths for raw captures (GET and POST /raw-captures, GET /raw-capture/{raw_capture_id}, PATCH /raw-capture/{raw_capture_id}/reject) by converting the Joi schemas with joi-to-swagger, and exports rawCaptureComponent listing the RawCapture fields such as session_id, lat, lon, image_url, status, rejection_reason and bulk_pack_file_name. The single-capture paths use the singular /raw-capture prefix while server/routes/rawCaptureRoutes.js mounts /raw-captures, and the reject operation documents the rejection body schema as a path parameter.
nodes.languageNotes: joi-to-swagger turns each Joi validation schema into an OpenAPI schema, so request docs stay derived from the same objects the handler validates with.

nodes.name: schemas.js
nodes.summary: Defines the Joi validation schemas for the raw capture endpoints: rawCaptureSchema for POST bodies (required uuid id and session_id, lat in -90..90, lon in -180..180, image_url URI, ISO captured_at, nullable step counts, rotation_matrix and unvalidated extra_attributes), rawCaptureGetQuerySchema (offset, limit, status of unprocessed/approved/rejected, bulk_pack_file_name), rawCaptureIdParamSchema and rawCaptureRejectionSchema (required rejection_reason plus integer organization_id for the legacy API call).

nodes.name: docs.js
nodes.summary: Builds the OpenAPI paths for sessions (GET and POST /session, GET /session/{session_id}) from the session Joi schemas via joi-to-swagger, and exports sessionComponent describing the Session fields such as start_time, bulk_pack_version, device_configuration_id, originating_wallet_registration_id, target_wallet, check_in_photo_url and track_url.

nodes.name: schemas.js
nodes.summary: Defines the Joi validation schemas for the session endpoints: sessionGetQuerySchema with filters on uuid ids, HH:MM start_time, YYYY-MM-DD created_at, organization_id arrays, offset/limit and whereNulls/whereNotNulls/whereIns arrays; sessionPostSchema requiring uuid id, device_configuration_id and originating_wallet_registration_id and restricting bulk_pack_version to v1 or v2; and sessionIdParamSchema for session_id.

nodes.name: swaggerDoc.js
nodes.summary: Assembles the OpenAPI 3.0.0 document titled 'Treetracker Field Data API' by merging the path objects from the device configuration, raw capture, session, wallet registration and track docs modules, registers the DeviceConfiguration, RawCapture, Session, WalletRegistration and Track component schemas, and reads the version from package.json. It also exports swaggerOptions with custom CSS that swaps the Swagger UI top-bar logo for assets/greenstand.webp, which server/app.js serves at /docs.

nodes.name: docs.js
nodes.summary: Builds the OpenAPI paths for wallet registrations (GET and POST /wallet-registration, GET /wallet-registration/{wallet_registration_id}) from the wallet registration Joi schemas via joi-to-swagger, and exports walletRegistrationComponent describing grower registration fields such as wallet, user_photo_url, grower_account_id, first_name, last_name, phone, email, lat, lon, registered_at and v1_legacy_organization.

nodes.name: schemas.js
nodes.summary: Defines the Joi validation schemas for wallet registration endpoints: walletRegistrationPostSchema requiring uuid id and grower_account_id, wallet, user_photo_url URI, first_name, last_name and bounded lat/lon, with nullable phone, an email that must contain '@', ISO registered_at and optional v1_legacy_organization; plus walletRegistrationIdParamSchema and a GET query schema limited to offset, limit and bulk_pack_file_name.

nodes.name: docs.js
nodes.summary: Builds the OpenAPI fragment for the track API: converts the Joi schemas from schemas.js with joi-to-swagger and exports trackSwagger (GET/POST /track and GET /track/{track_id}, with 201/200 responses that reference #/components/schemas/Track) plus trackComponent describing id, session_id, locations_url, created_at and bulk_pack_file_name. swaggerDoc.js merges both into the service's Swagger document.

nodes.name: index.js
nodes.summary: Express handlers for the track resource: trackPost validates the body and creates a track row (201), trackGet validates query filters and returns a paginated tracks list with prev/next links and a count, and trackSingleGet validates track_id and returns one track or a 404 HttpError. Each handler builds a new TrackService per request.

nodes.name: schemas.js
nodes.summary: Joi validation schemas for the track API: trackGetQuerySchema (optional offset >= 0, limit > 0, bulk_pack_file_name string, session_id uuid), trackPostSchema (required locations_url URI, session_id uuid and bulk_pack_file_name, no unknown keys) and trackIdParamSchema (required track_id uuid).

nodes.name: Track.js
nodes.summary: Domain model for the track table that wraps TrackRepository: lists tracks as frozen objects with id, locations_url, bulk_pack_file_name, session_id and created_at, counts tracks by filter, fetches one track by id and inserts a new track row.

nodes.name: TrackRepository.js
nodes.summary: Knex repository bound to the 'track' table; it adds nothing beyond the generic getById, getByFilter, countByFilter, update and create queries it inherits from BaseRepository.

nodes.name: trackRoutes.js
nodes.summary: Express router that mounts the track endpoints: POST /track to trackPost, GET /track to trackGet and GET /track/:track_id to trackSingleGet, each wrapped by handlerWrapper so async errors reach the error middleware. routes/index.js registers this router.

nodes.name: TrackService.js
nodes.summary: Service layer for tracks that opens a database Session and delegates list, count and get-by-id reads to the Track model; createTrack runs the insert inside an explicit transaction and rolls back on error.

nodes.name: trackPost
nodes.summary: Handles POST /track: validates req.body against trackPostSchema with abortEarly false, calls TrackService.createTrack to insert the track row and responds 201 with the created record.

nodes.name: trackGet
nodes.summary: Handles GET /track: validates query params, splits them into filter and limit options with getFilterAndLimitOptions, loads tracks and their total count from TrackService, and responds with tracks, prev/next links for the 'track' URL and the echoed query with count.

nodes.name: trackSingleGet
nodes.summary: Handles GET /track/:track_id: validates the track_id uuid, loads the track through TrackService.getTrackById and throws a 404 HttpError naming the id when no track with an id comes back.

nodes.name: Track
nodes.summary: Track model class built on a session-bound TrackRepository; its static Track() factory freezes the five public track fields, getTracks maps repository rows through that factory, while getTrackById and createTrack return raw repository rows and getTracksCount returns countByFilter.

nodes.name: TrackRepository
nodes.summary: Subclass of BaseRepository whose constructor passes the table name 'track' and the database session to the base class, so getById raises a 404 HttpError when no track row matches.

nodes.name: TrackService
nodes.summary: Creates a new Session and Track model per instance; exposes getTracks, getTracksCount and getTrackById as pass-through reads, and createTrack wraps the insert in beginTransaction/commitTransaction with rollback when a transaction is still in progress.

nodes.name: BaseSession.js
nodes.summary: Defines the BaseSession unit-of-work wrapper that holds one Knex instance and an optional open transaction in this.thx, so every repository that shares the session runs its queries either on the plain connection or inside the same transaction.

nodes.name: BaseSession
nodes.summary: Session base class: getDB() returns the open transaction or the raw Knex instance, isTransactionInProgress() checks thx, and beginTransaction/commitTransaction/rollbackTransaction throw 'Can not start transaction in transaction' or 'Can not commit/rollback transaction before start it!' on misuse and reset thx to undefined after commit or rollback.

nodes.name: LegacySession.js
nodes.summary: Exports LegacySession, a BaseSession bound to the knexLegacyDB connection from server/infra/database/knex.js, which RawCaptureService uses to write the legacy treetracker main DB tables trees and tree_attributes.

nodes.name: LegacySession
nodes.summary: Subclass whose constructor calls super(knexLegacyDB), so getDB() and its transaction methods target the legacy treetracker database instead of the field data database.

nodes.name: Session.js
nodes.summary: Exports Session, the default BaseSession bound to the field data Knex instance (knex from server/infra/database/knex.js, with the DATABASE_SCHEMA search path) that the field data services construct for their repositories and transactions.

nodes.name: Session
nodes.summary: Subclass whose constructor calls super(knex) with the field data database connection; it takes no arguments, so callers such as BaseRepository.spec.js that pass new Session(false) have the argument ignored.

nodes.name: WalletRegistration.js
nodes.summary: Wallet registration domain model that wraps WalletRegistrationRepository with a session and shapes rows into frozen objects with the grower fields id, wallet, user_photo_url, grower_account_id, first_name, last_name, phone, email, lat, lon, registered_at, bulk_pack_file_name and v1_legacy_organization; it also gives filtered listing, counting, lookup by id and idempotent creation.

nodes.name: WalletRegistration
nodes.summary: Model class holding a WalletRegistrationRepository built from the injected session; getWalletRegistrations maps getByFilter rows through _response, getWalletRegistrationsCount delegates to countByFilter, and getWalletRegistrationById filters on id and returns the first row or undefined.

nodes.name: WalletRegistration
nodes.summary: Static factory that picks the 13 wallet_registration response fields (from id and wallet through bulk_pack_file_name and v1_legacy_organization) out of a row and returns them as an Object.freeze'd value, dropping any other columns.

nodes.name: createWalletRegistration
nodes.summary: Idempotent insert: looks up the incoming id first and, when no row exists, creates it through the repository and returns { walletRegistration, status: 201 }; when the id already exists it returns the stored record with status 200 and writes nothing.

nodes.name: BaseRepository.spec.js
nodes.summary: Mocha unit tests for BaseRepository that mock the field data knex instance with mock-knex and assert the generated SQL against a 'testTable' table: getById, getByFilter with plain columns, a limit option and nested and/or filter objects, update, create with returning, and countByFilter parsing count '1' to 1; the getById 404 case and and/or support in countByFilter are skipped TODOs.
nodes.languageNotes: Each test reinstalls the mock-knex tracker and checks query.sql with regexes, so the tests verify the Knex SQL text without a live PostgreSQL database.

nodes.name: WalletRegistrationRepository.js
nodes.summary: Repository for the wallet_registration table; it only passes 'wallet_registration' and the session to BaseRepository, so wallet registrations use the generic getById, getByFilter, countByFilter, create and update queries.

nodes.name: WalletRegistrationRepository
nodes.summary: BaseRepository subclass whose constructor binds the table name 'wallet_registration' and the session, and sets _tableName and _session again after super() even though the base constructor already set them.

nodes.name: WalletRegistrationService.js
nodes.summary: Service layer for the wallet registration endpoints in server/handlers/walletRegistrationHandler: it creates one field data Session and a WalletRegistration model per service instance and wraps only the create path in a database transaction.

nodes.name: WalletRegistrationService
nodes.summary: Service class whose getWalletRegistrations, getWalletRegistrationsCount and getWalletRegistrationById pass straight through to the WalletRegistration model on a shared Session, while createWalletRegistration runs in a transaction.

nodes.name: createWalletRegistration
nodes.summary: Begins a transaction on the service Session, runs the model's idempotent createWalletRegistration (existence check plus insert), commits and returns { walletRegistration, status }; on any error it rolls back when isTransactionInProgress() is true and rethrows.

nodes.name: docs.js
nodes.summary: Builds the OpenAPI fragment for the device-configuration routes: GET and POST /device-configuration (201 on create, 200 on an existing id) and GET /device-configuration/{device_configuration_id}, with parameter and request schemas converted from the Joi schemas by joi-to-swagger. It also exports the DeviceConfiguration component with fields such as device_identifier, brand, model, serial, app_version, os_version, sdk_version, logged_at and bulk_pack_file_name.
nodes.languageNotes: joi-to-swagger derives the Swagger parameter schemas from the same Joi objects that the handlers use for validation, so docs and validation do not drift.

nodes.name: index.js
nodes.summary: Express handlers for the device-configuration resource: deviceConfigurationPost validates the body and returns 201 or 200 from DeviceConfigurationService, deviceConfigurationGet returns a paginated device_configurations list with prev/next links and count, and deviceConfigurationSingleGet returns one record or throws HttpError 404.

nodes.name: schemas.js
nodes.summary: Joi validation schemas for device configurations: the POST body requires a uuid id, device_identifier, brand, model, device, hardware, manufacturer, app_build, app_version, os_version, sdk_version and an ISO logged_at, allows an empty serial, and rejects unknown keys; also the uuid device_configuration_id path param and the offset/limit/bulk_pack_file_name list query.

nodes.name: DeviceConfiguration.js
nodes.summary: Domain model for device configurations that maps device_configuration rows to frozen objects and implements idempotent creation: createDeviceConfiguration looks up the id first and returns the existing row with status 200, or inserts it with a created_at timestamp and returns status 201.

nodes.name: DeviceConfigurationRepository.js
nodes.summary: Repository for the device_configuration PostgreSQL table; it only passes the table name and the Knex session to BaseRepository, which supplies getByFilter, countByFilter and create.

nodes.name: DeviceConfigurationService.js
nodes.summary: Service layer for device configurations that opens a new database Session per instance, delegates list, count and get-by-id reads to the DeviceConfiguration model, and wraps createDeviceConfiguration in a transaction with rollback on error.

nodes.name: deviceConfigurationPost
nodes.summary: POST /device-configuration handler: validates req.body against deviceConfigurationPostSchema with abortEarly false, calls createDeviceConfiguration and responds with the status (201 new, 200 existing) and the record.

nodes.name: deviceConfigurationGet
nodes.summary: GET /device-configuration handler: validates offset, limit and bulk_pack_file_name, fetches the filtered page and total count, and responds with device_configurations, prev/next links from generatePrevAndNext, and the echoed query with count.

nodes.name: deviceConfigurationSingleGet
nodes.summary: GET /device-configuration/{device_configuration_id} handler: validates the uuid path param, loads the record by id, and throws HttpError 404 with a not-found message when no record has an id.

nodes.name: DeviceConfiguration
nodes.summary: Model class over DeviceConfigurationRepository: a static factory freezes the 15 device fields plus created_at, list and count methods pass filters to the repository, and createDeviceConfiguration skips the insert when a row with the same id already exists.

nodes.name: DeviceConfigurationRepository
nodes.summary: BaseRepository subclass bound to the device_configuration table; its constructor only sets _tableName and _session and adds no custom queries.

nodes.name: DeviceConfigurationService
nodes.summary: Service class used by the device-configuration handlers; it owns a Session and a DeviceConfiguration model, and runs creation inside beginTransaction/commitTransaction with rollbackTransaction when a transaction is still in progress after an error.

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Single-entry Docker ignore list that keeps the host node_modules directory out of the build context, so the Dockerfile's COPY . ./ step does not overwrite the dependencies installed by npm ci inside the image.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Single-stage node:16-alpine image build for the field data API: it sets WORKDIR /app, adds /app/node_modules/.bin to PATH, copies package.json and package-lock.json, runs npm ci --silent, copies the source, and starts the service with node . (package.json main is server/server.js). The dev build-deploy workflow builds this file and pushes it as greenstand/<repo>:<version>.
nodes.languageNotes: The two package manifests are copied and npm ci runs before COPY . ./, so Docker reuses the cached dependency layer when only source files change. No EXPOSE or HEALTHCHECK is declared; the port comes from the runtime environment.

nodes.name: node
nodes.summary: The only build stage of the Dockerfile, based on node:16-alpine with no exposed ports, which produces the runtime container that runs server/server.js from /app.

nodes.name: pull-request-ci.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow 'CI for New Pull Requests' that runs on pull requests to main inside a node:20.16.0-alpine3.20 container with a postgis/postgis service. It runs npm ci, npm run lint (ESLint), npm run db-migrate-ci against DATABASE_URL, and npm run test with DATABASE_URL and DATABASE_URL_LEGACYDB both pointing at the same postgres service.
nodes.languageNotes: The job runs in a container, so the postgres service container is reached by its label hostname 'postgres' rather than localhost.

nodes.name: treetracker-api-build-deploy-dev.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions 'Service CI/CD Pipeline' on push to main: a test job repeats lint, db-migrate-ci and npm run test against a postgis service, then a release job (Greenstand repos only, skipped on 'skip-ci' commits) runs semantic-release, builds and pushes the Dockerfile image as greenstand/<repo>:<package.json version>, and uses kustomize to set that tag in deployment/overlays/development before it commits and pushes the bump.
nodes.languageNotes: The release job exports the version through the deprecated '::set-output' command and gates the kustomization commit on the head commit message not containing 'chore', which avoids a loop with semantic-release's own chore(release) commit.

nodes.name: treetracker-api-deploy-dev.yml
nodes.summary: Manual workflow_dispatch 'Deploy Service to Dev Env' that takes a git-tag input, runs kustomize edit set image in deployment/overlays/development to point greenstand/<repo> at that tag, and commits and pushes the change with a '[skip ci]' chore message.
nodes.languageNotes: The commit step is named 'Commit prod kustomization file' although it edits the development overlay, a copy-paste leftover from the prod workflow.

nodes.name: treetracker-api-deploy-prod.yml
nodes.summary: Manual workflow_dispatch 'Deploy Service to Prod Env' that promotes a given git-tag to production by running kustomize edit set image in deployment/overlays/production and pushing the resulting kustomization commit; it only runs in the Greenstand-owned repository.

nodes.name: treetracker-api-deploy-test.yml
nodes.summary: Manual workflow_dispatch 'Deploy Service to Test Env' that sets the greenstand/<repo> image tag in deployment/overlays/test to the git-tag input with kustomize and commits and pushes a '[skip ci]' bump, so the cluster GitOps sync rolls the test environment.

nodes.name: .env.example
nodes.summary: Template env file listing DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_SCHEMA (field_data) and DATABASE_URL_MAINDB with placeholder values. The legacy URL name is stale: config/config.js reads DATABASE_URL_LEGACYDB, not DATABASE_URL_MAINDB.

nodes.name: .env.test.example
nodes.summary: Template for the .env.test file that the mocha npm scripts load: DATABASE_URL and DATABASE_URL_SEEDER point at the shared DigitalOcean integration_test Postgres with {PASSWORD} and {SCHEMA} placeholders, plus NODE_LOG_LEVEL=debug. It omits DATABASE_URL_LEGACYDB and sets TREETRACKER_API_URL and REACT_APP_STAKEHOLDER_API_ROOT, which no server code reads.

nodes.name: .prettierrc.json
nodes.summary: Prettier formatting rules for the repo: semicolons on, trailing commas everywhere, single quotes. The npm prettier-fix and lint:fix scripts apply them.

nodes.name: CHANGELOG.md
nodes.summary: semantic-release changelog from 1.0.0 (2021-02-03) to 1.15.0 (2026-10-27, root check columns). It records the raw-capture reject endpoint (1.10.0), legacy admin API calls (1.10.1), bulk-pack v2 endpoints (1.7.0), tracks and session endpoints (1.12/1.13), session_segment tables (1.14.0) and many sealed-secret and kustomize deployment fixes.
nodes.languageNotes: Generated by semantic-release from conventional commits; entries mention RabbitMQ and event replay, which no longer exist in the runtime code.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Developer guide for the field data service: clone and npm install, dev DB passwords via doctl and scripts/setup-dev-database-passwords.sh, npm run server on port 3006, local Postgres with database/db_init.sql and db-migrate, and the protocol/service/model/repository layering. Some parts are stale: it names DATABASE_URL_LEGACYDB and RabbitMQ, a missing layers.png, a test-seedDB script and wallet API Postman specs.

nodes.name: api.json
nodes.summary: Early OpenAPI 3.0.3 draft (Jan 2021) for a /captures resource: GET with status, planter_contact, planter_id, limit (default 1000) and offset query parameters, empty POST and PATCH stubs, and a Capture schema with reference_id to the legacy trees table and attributes.entries key/value pairs. No code loads it; the live routes use /raw-captures and swaggerDoc.js builds the served spec from Joi schemas.

nodes.name: GET /captures
nodes.summary: Draft spec operation getCaptures that lists capture objects filtered by status, planter_contact and planter_id, paginated by limit and offset, with sample unverified captures that carry dbh, abs_step_count, delta_step_count and rotation_matrix attributes.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: npm manifest (name treetracker, version 1.15.0, Node >=16, main server/server.js) with Express, Knex/pg, Joi, joi-to-swagger, swagger-ui-express, axios, db-migrate and Sentry. Scripts run nodemon for the server, mocha with .env.test for __tests__ and repository specs, db-migrate-ci from database/, and knex seed:run for dev and usertest; app.js and swaggerDoc.js read its version field.
nodes.languageNotes: The test-unit glob targets server/models/**/*.spec.js and server-test targets server/serverTest.js; neither path exists at this commit.

nodes.name: 20201225201548-createCaptures-up.sql
nodes.summary: Initial field-data migration that creates the raw_capture table: uuid id, reference_id int8, image_url, numeric lat/lon, smallint gps_accuracy, field_user_id, field_username, field_user_photo_url, device_identifier, note, jsonb attributes, status, rejection_reason, and timestamptz created_at/updated_at, plus five btree indexes on status, field_user_id, field_username, created_at and updated_at.

nodes.name: 20201225201548-createCaptures-down.sql
nodes.summary: Rollback for the createCaptures migration: drops the five raw_capture indexes (rcapture_status_idx, rcapture_fieldusr_idx, rcapture_fieldusrname_idx, rcapture_crdate_idx, rcapture_update_idx) and then drops the raw_capture table itself.

nodes.name: 20201231060447-domainEvents-up.sql
nodes.summary: Creates the domain_event table (uuid id, jsonb payload, status, created_at, updated_at; composite primary key id+status+created_at) LIST-partitioned by status into raised, received, sent and handled, where sent and handled are further RANGE-partitioned by created_at into yearly 2021, 2022 and 2023 tables; adds a status index and a GIN jsonb_path_ops index on payload. No runtime code in this commit writes the table.
nodes.languageNotes: PostgreSQL declarative partitioning: a LIST partition (sent, handled) can itself be RANGE-partitioned, and the primary key must include every partition key column (status, created_at).

nodes.name: 20201231060447-domainEvents-down.sql
nodes.summary: Rollback for the domainEvents migration: drops event_status_idx and the GIN index event_pyld_idx, then drops the partitioned domain_event table, which removes its raised/received/sent/handled and yearly child partitions with it.

nodes.name: 20210513114937-addCaptureTakenColumn-up.sql
nodes.summary: Adds a nullable capture_taken_at timestamptz column to raw_capture so the service can record when the phone took the photo, separate from created_at.

nodes.name: 20210513114937-addCaptureTakenColumn-down.sql
nodes.summary: Reverts the addCaptureTakenColumn migration by dropping the capture_taken_at column from raw_capture.

nodes.name: 20210513233959-updateCaptureTakenColumn-up.sql
nodes.summary: Data backfill migration that runs UPDATE raw_capture SET capture_taken_at = created_at, so existing captures get a value before the column becomes NOT NULL.

nodes.name: 20210513233959-updateCaptureTakenColumn-down.sql
nodes.summary: Empty rollback for the updateCaptureTakenColumn backfill: it holds only the db-migrate placeholder comment, so a revert leaves the copied capture_taken_at values in raw_capture.

nodes.name: 20210513234014-modifyCaptureTakenColumn-up.sql
nodes.summary: Tightens raw_capture.capture_taken_at with ALTER COLUMN ... SET NOT NULL, after the previous migration backfilled the column from created_at.

nodes.name: 20210513234014-modifyCaptureTakenColumn-down.sql
nodes.summary: Empty rollback for the modifyCaptureTakenColumn migration: it holds only the placeholder comment, so the NOT NULL constraint on raw_capture.capture_taken_at stays after a revert.

nodes.name: 20220120081019-wallet-registration-up.sql
nodes.summary: Enables the uuid-ossp extension and creates the wallet_registration table: uuid id defaulting to uuid_generate_v4(), wallet, user_photo_url, grower_account_id uuid, first_name, last_name, optional phone and email, numeric lat/lon, registered_at timestamptz and optional v1_legacy_organization.

nodes.name: 20220120081019-wallet-registration-down.sql
nodes.summary: Rollback for the wallet-registration migration: a single DROP TABLE wallet_registration; it leaves the uuid-ossp extension installed.

nodes.name: 20220124224437-device-configuration-up.sql
nodes.summary: Creates the device_configuration table that stores the phone profile the Treetracker app reports: device_identifier, brand, model, device, serial, hardware, manufacturer, app_build, app_version, os_version, sdk_version (all NOT NULL varchar), logged_at timestamptz and created_at defaulting to now().

nodes.name: 20220124224437-device-configuration-down.sql
nodes.summary: Rollback for the device-configuration migration that runs DROP TABLE device_configuration.

nodes.name: 20220125153204-session-up.sql
nodes.summary: Creates the session table that links one upload session to its device and grower: uuid id, device_configuration_id foreign key to device_configuration(id), originating_wallet_registration_id foreign key to wallet_registration(id), optional target_wallet, check_in_photo_url, track_url, organization, and created_at defaulting to now().

nodes.name: 20220125153204-session-down.sql
nodes.summary: Rollback for the session migration that runs DROP TABLE session, removing the foreign keys to device_configuration and wallet_registration with it.

nodes.name: 20220126225534-bulk-pack-capture-updates-up.sql
nodes.summary: Reshapes raw_capture for the bulk-pack upload format: drops field_user_id, field_user_photo_url, field_username and device_identifier (now carried by session), adds session_id uuid referencing session(id), abs_step_count int, delta_step_count int and rotation_matrix int[], and renames attributes to extra_attributes.

nodes.name: 20220126225534-bulk-pack-capture-updates-down.sql
nodes.summary: Reverts the bulk-pack raw_capture reshape: re-adds field_user_id int8, field_user_photo_url, field_username and device_identifier as nullable columns, drops session_id, abs_step_count, delta_step_count and rotation_matrix, and renames extra_attributes back to attributes.

nodes.name: 20220227163837-rename-capture-taken-at-up.sql
nodes.summary: Renames raw_capture.capture_taken_at to captured_at, the column name that RawCaptureRepository selects and the raw capture API schema requires.

nodes.name: 20220227163837-rename-capture-taken-at-down.sql
nodes.summary: Reverts the column rename by changing raw_capture.captured_at back to capture_taken_at.

nodes.name: raw_capture
nodes.summary: Table definition for raw_capture as first created: one row per tree photo uploaded by a field user, with GPS lat/lon, image_url, reference_id, review status and rejection_reason; later migrations add captured_at and session_id and drop the field_user columns.

nodes.name: domain_event
nodes.summary: Table definition for domain_event, a status-partitioned jsonb event log with raised, received, sent and handled partitions and yearly 2021-2023 sub-partitions for sent and handled.

nodes.name: wallet_registration
nodes.summary: Table definition for wallet_registration: one row per grower wallet sign-up with names, phone, email, photo URL, grower_account_id, location and registered_at.

nodes.name: device_configuration
nodes.summary: Table definition for device_configuration: hardware and app version details (brand, model, serial, app_build, os_version, sdk_version) logged by each phone.

nodes.name: session
nodes.summary: Table definition for session: ties a device_configuration and an originating wallet_registration to a target_wallet, organization, check-in photo and track_url.

nodes.name: 20220304112209-change-rotation-matrix-down.sql
nodes.summary: Down migration that reverts raw_capture.rotation_matrix from float[] back to an integer array (int[]), which truncates the fractional device rotation values.

nodes.name: 20220304112209-change-rotation-matrix-up.sql
nodes.summary: Up migration that changes raw_capture.rotation_matrix from int[] to float[] so the capture's device rotation matrix keeps decimal precision; the raw capture handler validates it as an array of numbers.

nodes.name: 20220324190653-AddOrganizationIdToSession-down.sql
nodes.summary: Down migration that drops the organization_id column from the session table.

nodes.name: 20220324190653-AddOrganizationIdToSession-up.sql
nodes.summary: Up migration that adds a nullable organization_id varchar column to the session table, so a field session can record the organization it belongs to.

nodes.name: 20220411001144-addBulkPackFileName-down.sql
nodes.summary: Down migration that drops bulk_pack_file_name from the four upload tables raw_capture, wallet_registration, device_configuration and session.

nodes.name: 20220411001144-addBulkPackFileName-up.sql
nodes.summary: Up migration that adds a bulk_pack_file_name varchar column to raw_capture, wallet_registration, device_configuration and session, so each row records the uploaded bulk pack file it came from.

nodes.name: 20220601165814-change-gps-data-type-down.sql
nodes.summary: Down migration that narrows raw_capture.gps_accuracy back from numeric to smallint, dropping any decimal part of the accuracy value.

nodes.name: 20220601165814-change-gps-data-type-up.sql
nodes.summary: Up migration that widens raw_capture.gps_accuracy from smallint to numeric, so captures can store fractional GPS accuracy values sent by the app.

nodes.name: 20220618045205-add-wallet-registration-created-at-down.sql
nodes.summary: Down migration that drops the created_at column from the wallet_registration table.

nodes.name: 20220618045205-add-wallet-registration-created-at-up.sql
nodes.summary: Up migration that adds wallet_registration.created_at as timestamptz with DEFAULT now(), giving each wallet registration an insert timestamp.

nodes.name: 20221105211652-add-session-start-time-down.sql
nodes.summary: Down migration that drops the start_time column from the session table.

nodes.name: 20221105211652-add-session-start-time-up.sql
nodes.summary: Up migration that adds a nullable session.start_time timestamptz column; the session handler schema accepts it as an ISO date.

nodes.name: 20230302214605-bulk-pack-version-down.sql
nodes.summary: Down migration that drops the bulk_pack_version column from the session table.

nodes.name: 20230302214605-bulk-pack-version-up.sql
nodes.summary: Up migration that adds a session.bulk_pack_version varchar column; the session handler schema restricts its values to 'v1' or 'v2'.

nodes.name: 20230906143147-create-track-table-down.sql
nodes.summary: Down migration that drops the whole track table, deleting all stored session GPS track records.

nodes.name: 20230906143147-create-track-table-up.sql
nodes.summary: Up migration that creates the track table (uuid id, session_id FK to session, locations_url, bulk_pack_file_name, created_at timestamptz), which stores a pointer to each session's uploaded GPS track file.

nodes.name: 20240105095545-domainEventsNewPartition-down.sql
nodes.summary: Down migration that drops the six yearly partitions domain_event_sent_2024..2026 and domain_event_handled_2024..2026.

nodes.name: 20240105095545-domainEventsNewPartition-up.sql

tour.title: Process Entry Point
tour.description: The service starts in server/server.js, which package.json names as its main file. It loads the .env.<NODE_ENV> file, sets the log level, and starts the Express app on NODE_PORT (default 3006). On SIGINT, it destroys both Knex connection pools, one for the field-data database and one for the legacy treetracker database, which is a first sign that this service talks to two databases.
tour.languageLesson: In Node.js, the package.json "main" field tells `node .` which file to run. The Dockerfile in a later step starts the service with exactly that command.

tour.title: Express App Assembly
tour.description: server/app.js builds the Express application that server.js starts. It initializes Sentry, enables CORS only in development, rejects write requests without an application/json content type (HTTP 415), serves Swagger UI at /docs, mounts all routers at '/', and installs the global error handler. config/config.js maps DATABASE_URL and DATABASE_URL_LEGACYDB to the two connection strings that the data layer uses later.
tour.languageLesson: Express runs middleware in registration order. A function with four parameters (err, req, res, next) is an error-handling middleware, so app.js registers it after the routers to catch errors from all of them.

tour.title: Routers and Error Plumbing
tour.description: server/routes/index.js is a barrel that exports the five resource routers: raw captures, sessions, tracks, device configurations, and wallet registrations. Each router, such as rawCaptureRoutes.js, binds HTTP verbs to handler functions through handlerWrapper from utils.js. That wrapper forwards rejected promises to the errorHandler, which converts HttpError, Joi validation errors (422), and Axios errors into JSON {code, message} responses.
tour.languageLesson: Express 4 does not catch rejected promises from async handlers. A small higher-order function like handlerWrapper, `fn => (req, res, next) => fn(req, res, next).catch(next)`, closes that gap for every route in one place.

tour.title: Handlers and Joi Validation
tour.description: Handlers are the protocol layer: they validate input, call a service, and shape the HTTP response. The raw capture handler validates the Treetracker app upload with Joi schemas (UUID ids, lat/lon ranges, image URL, ISO captured_at) before it calls RawCaptureService. The list handlers share helper.js, which separates limit/offset (defaults 100 and 0) from filters and builds prev/next links.
tour.languageLesson: Joi schemas are declarative validators. A call to schema.validateAsync(body) either returns the cleaned value or throws a ValidationError, which the global errorHandler from Step 3 maps to HTTP 422.

tour.title: API Documentation Contract
tour.description: The Joi schemas from Step 4 also generate the API docs. Each handler folder has a docs.js that converts its schemas with joi-to-swagger, and swaggerDoc.js merges them into the 'Treetracker Field Data API' OpenAPI document that app.js serves at /docs. The hand-written spec under docs/api/spec is a separate reference copy, so check paths carefully: the generated raw capture docs use a singular /raw-capture prefix for single-capture paths while the router mounts /raw-captures.

tour.title: Service Layer
tour.description: Services own use cases and transactions. Most services, such as SessionService and WalletRegistrationService, open one field-data database session and wrap the create path in begin/commit/rollback. RawCaptureService is the most important one: it writes the legacy trees row and the field-data raw_capture row in paired transactions across two databases, and it rejects captures through LegacyAPIService, an HTTP client for the legacy admin API.

tour.title: Database Sessions and Knex
tour.description: The services from Step 6 do not use Knex directly. They use BaseSession, a unit-of-work wrapper that holds one Knex instance and an optional open transaction, so all repositories that share a session run in the same transaction. Session.js binds it to the field-data client, and LegacySession.js binds it to the legacy client. Both clients come from knex.js, which validates the connection strings and sets the DATABASE_SCHEMA search path on the field-data client only.
tour.languageLesson: The unit-of-work pattern passes one shared context object to many repositories. Knex makes this simple because a transaction object (trx) has the same query-builder API as the base knex instance.

tour.title: Domain Models
tour.description: Models sit between services and repositories and give each resource its business rules. They shape database rows into frozen objects and implement idempotent creation: if the id already exists, they return the stored row with status 200 instead of 201. This rule matters because the Treetracker app can upload the same capture, session, or registration more than once. RawCapture.js also sets new captures to 'unprocessed' and marks rejected ones 'rejected'.
tour.languageLesson: Object.freeze() makes an object shallowly immutable. Models return frozen objects so that callers cannot change a domain value by accident after it leaves the model.

tour.title: The Legacy Database Bridge
tour.description: During the domain migration, every new raw capture must also appear in the legacy treetracker database. LegacyTree.js resolves the planter by wallet (PlanterRepository) and writes the trees and tree_attributes rows, and TreeRepository inserts the tree with a PostGIS point. The ADR records a related bridge decision: a hand-filled session.organization_id that operators copy to the legacy trees.planting_organization_id until the Android app sends real organization keys.

tour.title: Repositories
tour.description: Repositories are the lowest code layer and the only place that builds SQL. BaseRepository, which every field-data and legacy repository extends, gives table-scoped getById, nested and/or filters with limit/offset, counts, update, and insert. Concrete repositories add joins: RawCaptureRepository and SessionRepository join session, wallet_registration, and device_configuration so that the API returns device and wallet details with each row.
tour.languageLesson: JavaScript classes support inheritance with `extends` and `super()`. A generic base class that receives the table name and session in its constructor removes most per-table boilerplate.

tour.title: Field Data Schema
tour.description: These tables are the data that the repositories from Step 10 read and write. A raw_capture is one tree photo with GPS data and a review status, and it belongs to a session. A session ties a device_configuration (the phone and app build) to the wallet_registration that started it, and a track stores the location file for a session. Note that raw_capture has the highest fan-in in the graph, because most of the code and later migrations depend on it.
tour.languageLesson: Foreign keys (for example session.device_configuration_id to device_configuration.id) make the database reject orphan rows. This is also why the test helper must delete tables in a foreign-key-safe order.

tour.title: Migrations and Local Setup
tour.description: The schema evolves through db-migrate: each JavaScript migration loads an up and a down SQL file, such as the newest one that adds root-check columns to raw_capture (no server code reads them at this commit). The README explains the local workflow: run database/db_init.sql, fill database.json from the example, run migrations, and start the server with npm run server. Some README parts are stale, so trust the code over the README when they disagree.
tour.languageLesson: Paired up/down migrations make schema changes reversible. Never edit a migration that already ran in a shared environment; add a new one instead.

tour.title: Integration Tests
tour.description: The tests exercise the full stack from Steps 2 to 11 through HTTP with Mocha and supertest. legacy-table-creation.js creates the legacy trees, tree_attributes, and planter tables, clear-db.js empties all tables before each suite, and insert-test-capture.js seeds the full planter, device, wallet, session, tree, and capture chain. The raw capture spec checks the idempotent 201/200 behavior and stubs LegacyAPIService with sinon for the reject path.
tour.languageLesson: A sinon stub replaces a real method for one test, so the test can check the arguments (here the Authorization header and rejection reason) without a call to the real legacy admin API.

tour.title: Container and Kubernetes Deployment
tour.description: The Dockerfile packages the service into a node:16-alpine image and starts it with `node .`, which runs server/server.js from Step 1. Kustomize manifests describe the cluster: the Deployment runs two replicas on port 3006 with both database URLs from a sealed secret, and a migration Job runs db-migrate up as an ArgoCD PostSync hook. The development, test, and production overlays only change the image tag and secrets.
tour.languageLesson: In a Dockerfile, copying package.json and package-lock.json and running npm ci before copying the source lets Docker cache the dependency layer, so code-only changes rebuild quickly.

tour.title: CI/CD Pipelines
tour.description: GitHub Actions close the loop. On each pull request, CI runs lint, the migrations, and the integration tests from Step 13 against a PostGIS service. On a push to main, the pipeline repeats the tests, runs semantic-release, pushes the Docker image from Step 14, and updates the development overlay tag. A manual workflow promotes a chosen git tag to production.
tour.languageLesson: A GitHub Actions `services:` block starts sidecar containers, such as a PostGIS database, that the job steps can reach by service name. This gives the tests a real database without extra setup scripts.
